extracted.intended_audience: PD/PI applicants to NIGMS and authorized organization representatives (AORs); institutional officials involved in NIH grant appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting appeals of referral/withdrawal decisions and of initial peer review decisions for applications to NIGMS, including required grounds, timing, routing, and possible outcomes. Applicable to PD/PIs and applicant institutions working with their AOR and NIGMS program officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of NIH appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has two formal appeals processes: to resolve disagreements between applicants and NIH staff concerning the referral (assignment) or withdrawal of applications prior to review; and to resolve disagreements between applicants and NIH review committees concerning review of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page covers both pre-review referral/withdrawal disputes and appeals of initial peer review (second-level appeals to NAGMS Council).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals during the referral process — assignment/dispute routing
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal of the study section or institute assignment (termed a 'dispute') before study section review of the application should be sent to the appropriate staff in the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). CSR's Division of Receipt and Referral (DRR) handles the initial referral of applications, and referral/review staff will respond to the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe your application was improperly assigned, address the dispute to CSR/DRR per their process and policy. Follow DRR's process and policy when DRR is the responsible party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals during the referral process — withdrawal routing (DRR vs NIGMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal of the withdrawal of an application prior to review will be handled by the withdrawing party: either DRR or NIGMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the withdrawal letter is signed by a Scientific Review Officer or a DRR Referral Officer, follow DRR's process and policy. If the withdrawal letter is signed by your Program Officer (PO), follow instructions in the withdrawal letter to begin the appeals process by reaching out to your PO; if discussion cannot resolve the issue, submit an appeal letter to your PO that includes both the reason for the withdrawal and why you believe the application should be reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-appeal consultation with NIGMS Program Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Before beginning the appeals process, the applicant is strongly advised to speak with the NIGMS PO responsible for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO can explain options and consequences, often helps applicants understand the study section's recommendation, and in most cases issues can be resolved through discussion without a formal appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit an appeal and required form of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is a written communication from a program director/principal investigator (PD/PI) and/or applicant institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be submitted in writing (appeal letter) and should include required institutional concurrence (see AOR concurrence metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal letter eligibility criteria (four required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter must: 1) be received after issuance of the summary statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review (NAGMS Council), 2) describe a flaw or perceived flaw in the review process for a particular application, 3) display concurrence from the AOR, and 4) be based on one or more of the specified issues related to the process of the initial peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals that do not meet all these criteria and/or do not include the concurrence of the AOR will not be considered an appeal letter but rather a grievance, and will not necessarily be taken to the NAGMSC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: evidence of reviewer bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of bias on the part of one or more peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bias is an acceptable ground for appeal if it is evidence-based and could have affected the review process/outcome. Provide concrete examples/documentation in the appeal letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: conflict of interest (COI) per regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict of interest (COI), as specified in regulation at 42 CFR 52h.5 'Scientific Peer Review of Research Grant Applications and Research and Development Contract Projects,' on the part of one or more peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If alleging COI, identify the alleged conflict and explain how it violated the regulation and affected the review. Appeals involving potential COI by NIH staff or other federal employees are referred to the appropriate deputy ethics counselor (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: lack of appropriate expertise in review panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of appropriate expertise within the review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document why the panel lacked the necessary expertise and how that deficiency materially affected the evaluation of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: factual errors by reviewer(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual error(s) made by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the outcome of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the factual error(s), provide correct factual information, and explain how the error(s) could have changed scoring or the review recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not an acceptable ground: differences in scientific opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal letters based solely on differences of scientific opinion will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disagreements about scientific judgment or interpretation are not appealable; appeals must allege a process flaw of the types enumerated (bias, COI, lack of expertise, factual error).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and internal handling of appeal letters after study section review
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter submitted after the study section review should be sent to the NIGMS PO. The letter will be shared with the Scientific Review Officer (SRO), who will respond in writing to the PO. Program and review staff will try to resolve the issues and take appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If staff cannot resolve the issues, the appeal letter and all relevant information are made available to the NAGMSC for second-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/deadline for Council consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals are due 30 calendar days before the applicable Council meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of appeals received after this date may be deferred to the next Council meeting. Note also the earlier eligibility timing requirement: appeals must be submitted after issuance of the summary statement and within the specified Council-related window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible outcomes and consequences of Council review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council may agree with either the study section or the applicant. If the Council agrees with the applicant, it recommends appropriate action to resolve the matter; if it agrees with the study section, the applicant may decide to submit a new or revised application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a re-review is recommended, the same application, not a revised or updated version, will be re-evaluated. The Council's recommendation concerning the resolution of an appeal is final and will not be reconsidered by the NIH through this or another process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contacting Council members
rubrics_metrics.description: At no time should the PD/PI or an official of the applicant organization attempt to contact individual Council members to discuss the application or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting Council members could jeopardize the confidentiality and integrity of the appeals process and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification as grievance if criteria not met
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter that does not meet the appeal criteria and/or does not include concurrence of the AOR will not be considered an appeal letter but rather a grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievances will not necessarily be taken to the NAGMSC; they may be handled differently and are less likely to result in formal Council action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of appeals alleging COI or staff ethical violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals involving potential COI or violation of ethical conduct rules on the part of an NIH staff member or other federal employee will be referred to the appropriate deputy ethics counselor for consideration and resolution before any further review of or action on the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such referrals may delay or change the subsequent handling of the appeal; follow any instructions resulting from the ethics review.
